agenda_items.title: Saskatoon Homelessness Action Plan 2026 [CC2026-0301]
agenda_items.content: Director of Planning and Development Anderson presented the report and responded to a question of Committee. Karen Kobussen, Saskatoon West Business Association, expressed concerns with the effectiveness of existing approaches to addressing homelessness and encouraged consideration of alternative strategies, enhanced performance measurement, and a greater focus on achieving measurable outcomes. She responded to questions of Committee. Rob Wilgenhof expressed support for the City's efforts to address homelessness and addictions and encouraged consideration of additional community-based response measures to complement existing emergency services. Mathieu Gaudet, Métis Nation–Saskatchewan, expressed support of the Plan highlighting the collaborative development of the plan, emphasized the importance of coordinated efforts among partners, and encouraged continued support for implementation of the plan's priorities and actions. He responded to questions of Committee. Gordon Taylor, Executive Director, The Salvation Army, expressed support for the Plan and highlighted the importance of a range of housing and shelter options, as well as continued investment in services and supports to assist individuals experiencing homelessness. He responded to questions of Committee. Colleen Christopherson-Cote, Saskatoon Poverty Reduction Partnership, spoke in support of the Plan emphasizing the importance of a coordinated, community-wide approach to addressing homelessness and poverty and highlighted the need for continued collaboration across sectors to achieve long-term outcomes. She responded to questions of Committee. Jodie Semkiw, Executive Director, Saskatoon Crisis Intervention Service, spoke in support of the Plan highlighting the importance of housing stability, coordinated community services, and ongoing supports for individuals with complex needs, and emphasized the value of collaboration in addressing homelessness. She responded to questions along with Tammy MacFarlane.  Discussion continued. City Manager Jorgenson and Director Anderson responded to questions of Committee. The meeting recessed at 11:28 a.m. and reconvened at 11:42 a.m. with all members in attendance with the exception of Councillor Davies.  Questions to the administration continued. Robert Lafontaine, Saskatoon Housing Initiatives Partnership, was in the gallery and was called forward to respond to questions of Committee regarding homelessness data collection, reporting practices, and ongoing efforts to improve data sharing and coordination among community partners.
agenda_items.recommendation: That the Governance and Priorities Committee recommend to City Council: That this report and the Saskatoon Homelessness Action Plan 2026 be received as information; That City Council reaffirm the City of Saskatoon's leadership role and specific actions within the Saskatoon Homelessness Action Plan, as previously approved by City Council on July 30, 2025; That the performance indicators contained within the Saskatoon Homelessness Action Plan be endorsed as the framework for monitoring, evaluating and reporting on progress related to the City of Saskatoon's approved role and actions within the Plan; and That any municipal budget requests associated with the Saskatoon Homelessness Action Plan be brought forward for consideration through future budget requests.
agenda_items.vote_detail: In Favour (10) Councillor Parker, Mayor Block, Councillor Donauer, Councillor Dubois, Councillor Ford, Councillor Jeffries, Councillor Kelleher, Councillor MacDonald, Councillor Pearce, and Councillor Timon Absent (1) Councillor Davies CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY
